surface_recreation_leak_check.command: Five HOME -> relaunch surface recreation cycles with dumpsys meminfo after each cycle; then force-stop and inspect logcat.
surface_recreation_leak_check.markers: 8 SurfaceRuntime destroy complete events and 9 Dawn initialized events; no FATAL EXCEPTION or Fatal signal.
surface_recreation_leak_check.native_pss_kb: ~30,584 before the first probe; ~129,689 after eight cycles (about +12 MB per recreation).
surface_recreation_leak_check.follow_up_experiment: Two temporary teardown experiments were tested and reverted: wgpu::Device::Destroy() before Dawn handle release, and Skia Context::freeGpuResources() after synchronous completion. Neither changed the observed growth: a five-cycle run still rose from 42,969 KB to 92,549 KB native PSS. The experiments are not part of the committed five-file Android scope. The Android lifecycle-lock fix was then built and exercised for five more cycles; native PSS still rose from 42,905 KB to 92,553 KB, confirming the growth is not caused by an overwritten HandlerThread pair.
surface_recreation_leak_check.classification: GPU lifecycle is functional, but repeated surface recreation retains substantial native memory. The growth persists after explicit Dawn device destruction and Skia resource purging, so full B3 leak acceptance is failed and the root cause likely requires common Dawn/Skia or emulator-driver investigation outside this isolated five-file Android slice.

lifecycle_thread_ownership_fix.change: Serialize surfaceCreated and surfaceDestroyed with a lifecycle lock so callbacks cannot overwrite the renderThread/Handler pair during teardown.
lifecycle_thread_ownership_fix.probe: No duplicate surfaceCreated warning; each observed surfaceDestroyed reported render thread stopped. Native PSS growth remained unchanged, so this fixes the callback race defensively but not the GPU-memory blocker.

bounded_leak_investigation.classification: The branch-owned Kotlin/SurfaceRuntime teardown completed for every measured cycle, and the growth is in native heap with zero Graphics PSS. The prior explicit wgpu::Device::Destroy and Skia freeGpuResources experiments did not change the slope. No safe five-file Android lifecycle fix is supported by this evidence; the allocation pattern is escalated as common Dawn/Skia or emulator Vulkan-driver retention.
bounded_leak_investigation.follow_up: Common render-toolchain/emulator-driver owner must reproduce with a clean process, identify the 4718592-byte allocation class, and provide a Dawn/Skia or emulator-driver fix and before/after counters. B3 remains blocked until that evidence exists.
